sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Paikas**: Hereditary landed militia of the Gajapati rulers of Odisha, who held rent-free lands (**Nish-kar**) in exchange for military service.
• **British Policy**: Post-1803 conquest, the British replaced the traditional land tenure with the **Permanent Settlement**, leading to the resumption of Paika lands.
• **Economic Catalyst**: Introduction of **Salt Tax** and the requirement to pay revenue in **silver/cash** crippled the local economy.
• **Key Metric**: The rebellion was led by **Bakshi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar**, the former commander of the forces of the Raja of Khurda.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Khurda, Odisha; Displacement of traditional landed gentry
Resumption of rent-free lands and high taxation
Mains: Link to colonial land revenue impact
Bakshi Jagabandhu's leadership; Alliance with local tribals
Loss of status and livelihood of the Paika class
Prelims: Identification of key leaders and timeline

items.definition: Rent-free lands granted to Paikas for their military service; their resumption by the British was the primary trigger for the rebellion.
The military commander of the Khurda Raja who became the face of the rebellion; he is often recognized as a national hero in Odisha.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **1817 Uprising**: The rebellion spread rapidly from Khurda to Puri and Cuttack, involving the Paikas, Kandhas, and local zamindars.
• **British Response**: The rebellion was suppressed by 1825, followed by the appointment of a commission to investigate the grievances.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of modern weaponry and centralized coordination compared to the British military.
• **Historical Recognition**: Recent debates on whether to classify it as the 'First War of Independence' (1817 vs 1857).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content: • **Memory Acronym**: 'P-A-I-K-A' (P-olicy of Land, A-dministrative displacement, I-ncreased Salt Tax, K-hurda base, A-nti-British).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Paika Rebellion (1817) with the Chuar or Paik rebellion of Bengal. Ensure you distinguish the Odisha-based Paika Rebellion from other tribal uprisings.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Colonial Agrarian Imperialism' to describe the root cause of the Paika Rebellion.

keyTakeaways: The Paika Rebellion was a reaction to the disruption of the traditional land-tenure system.
It was not merely a peasant revolt but a military-led uprising against colonial administrative changes.
The rebellion highlights the transition from traditional feudal military structures to modern colonial state control.
